## Introductions {.unlisted .unnumbered .html-hidden .discussion-slide}

Introduce yourself in one minute:

1. Name, discipline, and supervisor
2. Stage of your doctorate (e.g., cumulative or monograph, papers published or under review)
3. The manuscript you brought and its target outlet

# Contribution Sentence {.headline-only}

## Contribution Clarity

:::medium
If you cannot state your contribution in one sentence, you do not have it yet.
:::

> We contribute by [mechanism or boundary condition] explaining [X → Y] for [literature or audience].

:::notes
@thatcher2025rules includes contribution clarity in the diagnostics box [Appendix E]. The template forces three decisions: what the paper adds (a mechanism or a boundary condition), which relationship it explains, and for whom the explanation matters. You write a first version at the start of the course and revise it at the end of the first day, after the desk-reject simulation and the assumption hunt.
:::

## Elevator Pitch {.unlisted .unnumbered .html-hidden .discussion-slide}

:::medium
Can you state your contribution in one sentence?
:::

> We contribute by [mechanism or boundary condition] explaining [X → Y] for [literature or audience].

:::incremental
1. Write your sentence (3 minutes).
2. Read it aloud; the group asks one clarifying question each.
3. Keep the sentence; you revise it at the end of the day.
:::

:::notes
Most participants struggle to fill all three slots of the template; the gaps that appear here are the starting point for the first day.
:::
